I've been farming here in Quzhou for 35 years, so I know my land well. With 18.4 mu and high school behind me, I plan carefully — I read the county extension notices, I talk to the cooperative agronomist, and I also trust what my own eyes have seen in past seasons.

My main system is cotton because the soil here suits it and prices have been steady enough. I'll put 10 mu into cotton this year. The remaining 8.4 mu I keep in the traditional winter wheat–summer maize rotation — that way I have grain for the household and don't put all my eggs in one basket. With only 2 of us at home and some off-farm income, I can afford to invest properly in inputs, but I still watch costs — fertilizer prices jumped again this year.

**Cotton (10 mu, planted late April):** I use hybrid Bt varieties — the bollworm pressure here has come down a lot since we all switched. I plan about 12 kg N per mu, split: base fertilizer before planting, then topdress at squaring and flowering. Too much N and the plants grow tall with few bolls — I learned that the hard way back around 2005. Phosphorus 6 kg/mu and potassium 10 kg/mu — cotton really needs potassium for boll filling, and our soil runs low on it. I'll irrigate about 4 times from the well: after planting, bud stage, flowering, and boll-forming. Cotton needs many sprays — aphids, spider mites, lygus, cotton bollworm — I budget for 8 applications. Plough before planting to break the pan. Target yield 260 kg/mu seed cotton, which is realistic for my fields.

**Winter wheat (8.4 mu, sown early October):** Improved variety, Jimai or Shixin line — everyone around here uses these. 14 kg N/mu, split between base and spring topdressing at jointing. 7 kg P and 5 kg K. Three irrigations: pre-sowing, spring green-up, and grain-filling. Two pesticide sprays — one for aphids/powdery mildew at heading, one for rust if it shows up. Plough tillage after the maize, with stubble incorporation. I expect 480 kg/mu.

**Summer maize (8.4 mu, sown mid-June right after wheat harvest):** Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Denghai series. 15 kg N/mu — maize is hungry for N — most as topdressing at large flare stage. 5 kg P, 5 kg K. Two irrigations: at tasseling and grain-filling if rain is short. Two sprays for corn borer and armyworm. No-tillage direct seeding into the wheat stubble saves me time and moisture. Target 580 kg/mu.
